extracted.intended_audience: higher-education communications and marketing professionals (institutional and unit-level communicators); university administrators
extracted.subtask_description: Benchmarks and evaluative criteria for campus communications and marketing programs, including strategic messaging, identity standards, organizational structure, channels, audience targeting and measurement. Geared to assess and improve communications at institutional and unit levels in higher education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of a strategic communications plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Does your institution have a strategic communications plan? (Survey question: 'Does your institution have a strategic communications plan?')
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose of a plan: coordinate campuswide strategic communications planning; strengthen the university brand; unify key themes and messages; maximize use of available research and resources; identify and propagate best practices and cost-effective communications strategies. Survey scale: Yes / No / Unsure. Notes: nearly half of respondents indicated plans exist; unit-level communicators are often less aware of institutional plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presence of clearly articulated key messages
rubrics_metrics.description: Does your institution have clearly articulated key messages? (Survey question: 'Does your institution have clearly articulated key messages?')
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of strong messages provided in the report (e.g., 'Pacific is Personal', 'Freedom to Flourish', 'Better living for all'). Guidance includes embedding messages in the institution’s identity platform to communicate mission, values and vision. Survey scale: Yes / No / Unsure. Tools to promote clarity: brand sheets, crib sheets, 'brand kit', Communicators Council meetings, staff assistance, templates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effectiveness of communicating key messages to internal audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Has your institution been effective in communicating its key messages to internal audiences? (Survey question with response options Effective / Somewhat effective / Not effective / Unsure)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this dimension to evaluate internal reach and uptake of strategic messages. Findings: 25% rated internal communication effective, 67% somewhat effective, 7% not effective. Guidance: track differences by institutional vs unit-level respondents as unit-level staff may feel less informed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effectiveness of communicating key messages to external audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: How effective is the institution in communicating its key messages to external audiences? (Survey question with response options Effective / Somewhat effective / Not effective / Unsure)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to evaluate brand/messaging resonance with alumni, donors, prospective students, media, parents, legislators. Findings: respondents rated external effectiveness somewhat higher than internal in some areas. Consider targeted tactics per audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of identity standards (logo, seal, colors, typefaces, templates)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does your institution have guidelines or identity standards regarding the use of its official logo, seal and school colors? (Survey question)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identity standards typically include where/how to use the institution’s logo, approved color palettes and typefaces, and stipulations for templates (letterhead, business cards, web pages, brochures). Survey scale: Yes / No / Unsure. Finding: 96% indicated standards exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effectiveness of communicating identity standards to campus community
rubrics_metrics.description: Has your institution been effective in communicating its identity standards to the campus community? (Survey question with response options Effective / Somewhat effective / Not effective / Unsure)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to assess awareness and understanding of visual/brand rules. Finding: nearly 60% rated communication of identity standards as 'somewhat effective'; 30% 'effective'. Consider targeted training and examples to improve understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to identity standards (compliance frequency)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do communicators and others on campus adhere to your institution's identity standards? (Survey options Often / Sometimes / Rarely / Unsure)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure actual compliance in use of logos/colors/templates. Finding: 49.8% 'Often', 46.5% 'Sometimes'. Use compliance checks, approvals and procurement controls to increase adherence. Note: social media is a new compliance challenge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement of identity standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Is compliance with the institution's identity standards enforced? (Survey question Yes / No / Unsure; if yes, describe how)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of enforcement: central office approval of printed products, dedicated printer requiring compliance, purchasing-level compliance checks, review and approval during production. Finding: 44% reported enforcement exists, 39% said no, 16% unsure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring awareness/compliance with identity standards
rubrics_metrics.description: How is overall awareness of and compliance with the institution's identity standards monitored, if at all? (select all that apply: It is not monitored / Surveys / Audits / Other)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use formal monitoring (surveys, audits) to measure compliance; many institutions report limited monitoring. Finding: 59% 'not monitored', 39% 'audits', 7% 'surveys'. Monitoring supports enforcement and improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation of identity standards' impact on target audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: How is effectiveness evaluated of your institution's identity standards in terms of impact on targeted audiences? (select all that apply: It is not evaluated / Surveys / Focus Groups / Other)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This measures whether identity standards lead to desired audience perceptions. Finding: 63.5% said 'not evaluated'; 29.2% use surveys and focus groups. Recommendation: use surveys/focus groups to assess recognition, clarity and brand impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communications organizational structure model
rubrics_metrics.description: Which best describes the communications structure at your institution? (Centralized / Decentralized / Hybrid)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions: Centralized — managed from central office; Decentralized — colleges/units conduct independent efforts; Hybrid — combination. Use to evaluate which model supports strategic messaging and resource allocation. Finding: 63% hybrid, 23% centralized, 13% decentralized; larger institutions trend toward hybrid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effectiveness of media relations (institution and unit levels)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rate the overall effectiveness of media relations at both the institution-level and at the unit/college-level (survey matrix).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure media relations separately for institution and unit levels; expect differences in perceived effectiveness. Findings: institutional communicators rated institutional media relations higher than unit-level communicators did for the same activities. Use separate strategies and support for unit-level media work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effectiveness of electronic communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Rate the overall effectiveness of electronic communications at institution and unit levels (survey matrix).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electronic/web communications are among the most frequently performed activities. Evaluate usability, content strategy, and integration with messaging. Compare institution- and unit-level performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effectiveness of institutional branding
rubrics_metrics.description: Rate the overall effectiveness of institutional branding at institution and unit levels (survey matrix).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutional branding is consistently rated highly. Use brand standards and examples to maintain consistent application across units; brand management often centralizes key elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effectiveness of consistent messaging
rubrics_metrics.description: Rate the overall effectiveness of producing and sustaining consistent messaging at institution and unit levels (survey matrix).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistent messaging supports unified impressions. Tools to improve consistency include web/publication templates, staff assistance, examples of successful compliance, and regular Communicators Council meetings. Monitor alignment between institutional priorities and unit priorities to reduce fragmentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effectiveness of printed communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Rate the overall effectiveness of printed communications at institution and unit levels (survey matrix).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unit-level printed publications are often rated more effective by unit communicators than by institutional communicators. Consider review/approval workflows and quality standards, especially for institutions that route print through central production or approved vendors to enforce compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effectiveness of social networking
rubrics_metrics.description: Rate the overall effectiveness of social networking (social media) at institution and unit levels (survey matrix).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Social networking effectiveness varies by audience; Facebook and Twitter are now considered among the most effective channels for alumni/donors, current students and prospective students. Social media introduces new identity compliance issues and requires specific guidance/policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effectiveness of internal communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Rate the overall effectiveness of internal communications at institution and unit levels (survey matrix).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Internal communications often perceived as ineffective, especially in decentralized models. Effective internal tactics include e-mail, web pages, internal newsletters and regular meetings. Alignment and two-way communication between institutional and unit communicators is critical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Range of communications activities performed
rubrics_metrics.description: Which communications activities are performed by communicators? (list includes Advertising, Alumni/dev publications, Brand management, Broadcast, Community relations, Electronic/Web, Direct mail, Government relations, Graphic design, Institutional relations, Internal communications, Marketing, Media relations, News bureau, Photography, Publication services, Public relations, Printing services, Research publications, Special events, Student publications, University relations, Videography)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this dimension to benchmark staffing, roles and breadth of responsibilities. Findings: most frequently performed activities include electronic/web communications, marketing, media relations, public relations, brand management and publications. Many communicators 'wear many hats'—plan staffing accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frequency of communications by target audience
rubrics_metrics.description: How frequently does your communications program communicate with target audiences? (audiences: Alumni & donors, Parents, Current students, Prospective students, Faculty, Faculty of other institutions, Staff, Legislators, Campus administrators, Media; response options Frequently / Sometimes / Rarely)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use frequency benchmarks to align resources and priorities. Findings: alumni/donors and media are among the most frequently targeted; parents and legislators less so. Compare frequency against strategic priorities to ensure alignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perceived effectiveness of specific communications channels by audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondents' opinions on effectiveness of specific communications channels by target audience (channels: E-mail, Postcards, Direct mail brochures, Letters, Telephone, Web pages, Magazine, Poster, Newsletter, Radio, Television, Flyers, Outdoor, Facebook, Twitter, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use channel-audience matrix to select tactics: Facebook/Twitter effective for alumni/donors and students; email/web pages/internal newsletters for faculty & staff; telephone and e-mail for media. Leverage channel strengths per audience and measure outcomes. The survey reports channel-specific effectiveness percentages by audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring/evaluation of communications effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: How is the effectiveness of communications programs monitored? (select all that apply: Effectiveness is not monitored / Surveys / Focus groups / Response rates / Informal feedback / Other)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal monitoring (surveys, focus groups) is used by fewer than half of respondents; many rely on informal feedback or response rates. Use a combination of formal and informal metrics (response rates, surveys, audits, focus groups) to quantify effectiveness. Surveyed reporting: 14.5% 'not monitored', 44.4% 'surveys', 27.4% 'focus groups', 49.0% 'response rates', 76.6% 'informal feedback'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Barriers to effective communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Common barriers identified by respondents (leadership, staffing, funding, lack of coordination, lack of inclusion of unit communicators, size of institution, volume of materials, outdated visual/editorial modes, top-down decision-making).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this dimension to diagnose obstacles to strategic communications. Representative quotes in the report highlight problems: 'A lack of leadership that believe in strategic communication plans', 'Staff — we simply don't have the staff to do the work', 'Lack of teamwork and cooperation among key units', 'Upper administration not sharing information', 'Size of institution sometimes hampers clarity of message'. Recommendations include improving leadership buy-in, staffing/resources, inclusion in planning, and better information-sharing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resources and tools offered to aid compliance and consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Which resources are offered by the institution to aid colleges/units with compliance? (Web templates, Brochure templates, Publication templates, Online FAQ, Staff assistance, Examples of successful compliance, Other)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these tools to improve consistent application of key messages and identity standards. Findings: high prevalence of web templates (79%), staff assistance (91%), and other templates/examples. Good practices include weekly Communicators Council meetings, brand kits, crib sheets, and one-on-one support for smaller institutions.
